literal: Than themselves, their children's possession of wisdom, on the great earth, to enduring living beings all, is sweet.
translation: That their children possess wisdom greater than their own is a joy to all living beings on this great earth.
modern: தம்மை விடத் தம் பிள்ளைகள் அறிவுடையவர்களாக இருப்பது, இந்தப் பெரிய உலகத்தில் உள்ள எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் மகிழ்ச்சி தருவதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet expresses the universal joy of seeing the next generation surpass the current one. The word 'tammin' means 'than themselves', setting up a comparison between the parents and their children. 'Arivudaimai' denotes the possession of wisdom. The poet states that on this great earth, it is a sweet and natural joy for all living beings to see their offspring possess greater wisdom than they do. This highlights that the desire for one's children to excel is a fundamental trait of all life.
